From a55c2a5c8d680156495b7b1e2a9f5a3e313ba524 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Alessio Belle <alessio.belle@imgtec.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 15:23:48 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] drm/imagination: Fix deadlock in soft reset sequence

The soft reset sequence is currently executed from the threaded IRQ
handler, hence it cannot call disable_irq() which internally waits
for IRQ handlers, i.e. itself, to complete.

Use disable_irq_nosync() during a soft reset instead.

Fixes: cc1aeedb98ad ("drm/imagination: Implement firmware infrastructure and META FW support")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Alessio Belle <alessio.belle@imgtec.com>
Reviewed-by: Matt Coster <matt.coster@imgtec.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260309-fix-soft-reset-v1-1-121113be554f@imgtec.com
Signed-off-by: Matt Coster <matt.coster@imgtec.com>

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/imagination/pvr_power.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/imagination/pvr_power.c
index 0cf7393f89c6..ab10b4ac06b0 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/imagination/pvr_power.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/imagination/pvr_power.c
@@ -510,7 +510,16 @@ pvr_power_reset(struct pvr_device *pvr_dev, bool hard_reset)
 	}
 
 	/* Disable IRQs for the duration of the reset. */
-	disable_irq(pvr_dev->irq);
+	if (hard_reset) {
+		disable_irq(pvr_dev->irq);
+	} else {
+		/*
+		 * Soft reset is triggered as a response to a FW command to the Host and is
+		 * processed from the threaded IRQ handler. This code cannot (nor needs to)
+		 * wait for any IRQ processing to complete.
+		 */
+		disable_irq_nosync(pvr_dev->irq);
+	}
 
 	do {
 		if (hard_reset) {
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

The patch modifies a single file: `drivers/gpu/drm/imagination/pvr_power.c`. The change is in the `pvr_power_reset()` function, which was previously calling `disable_irq()` unconditionally. This call blocks until all pending IRQ handlers complete, causing a deadlock when the function is executed from the threaded IRQ handler itself (as happens during a soft reset).

The fix distinguishes between hard and soft resets:
- **Hard reset**: continues to use `disable_irq()` (blocking wait is safe).
- **Soft reset**: now uses `disable_irq_nosync()` (non-blocking) to avoid waiting for the current IRQ handler to finish, since the soft reset routine is already running in that handler.

## Relationships Between Modifications

- The logical structure of the reset function is preserved, but the `disable_irq` call is split into two conditional paths based on the `hard_reset` parameter.
- The change directly resolves a deadlock: the original single-path code would hang when a soft reset was triggered from the threaded IRQ context because `disable_irq` waits for the very handler that is currently executing the reset.
- The new code maintains full functionality for hard resets (where blocking is acceptable) while fixing the soft reset scenario.
